thread:
mika: Heads-up  noticed a per-model cost spike on the cost dashboard that lines up with yesterday's quota ramp. Seems concentrated on the prefetch route. :thinking:
dev: which model/tenants?
mika: mainly beta-gnome (m-medium-1) and ~10 low-latency tenants in the canary group. dashboard rows show cache_offset=0 for many entries even though traces show prefetch hits.
ops: interesting. router logs for the same window show `x-redwood-route: prefetch` repeatedly. however econ ingest shows no `x-cache-credit` present on those invocations.
lina: did we rename the header in last week's release? i recall a change to `x-rw-cache-credit` to standardize across private deploys.
dev: if header name changed, our econ parser would ignore credits. can someone grep the audit logs for both headers?
ops: quick grep output:
```
# router-audit.log
2026-04-06T14:02:11Z tenant=42 id=inv_abc x-redwood-route=prefetch x-rw-cache-credit=150
2026-04-06T14:02:12Z tenant=42 id=inv_def x-redwood-route=prefetch
2026-04-06T14:02:13Z tenant=43 id=inv_ghi x-redwood-route=prefetch x-rw-cache-credit=120
```
ops: you can see some invocations have `x-rw-cache-credit` while others don't. looks inconsistent for the cohort.
mika: UX problem: when credits are missing we currently show the raw token cost which spikes the product owners and can trigger pages. we should show an explicit "credits pending" state and an estimated post-credit unit cost.
lina: agree. proposal: dashboard changes - add columns `applied_credits` and `post_credit_unit_cost`, and a lightweight banner for the affected time window saying "crediting under investigation" with a link to the ticket.
sam: backend plan: make econ-ingest tolerant of both `x-cache-credit` and `x-rw-cache-credit` (mapping layer), and add a reconciliation job that backfills credits for a 48h window where the router tag exists but credits are missing. SQL sketch:```-- backfill estimated credits
insert into econ_adjustments (invocation_id, credit, reason, created_by)
select i.id, coalesce(a.estimated_credit, 0), 'prefetch-header-mapping', 'reconciler-v1'
from invocations i
left join prefetch_audit a on a.invocation_id = i.id
where i.ts > now() - interval '48 hours'
  and i.route = 'prefetch'
  and not exists (select 1 from econ_adjustments e where e.invocation_id = i.id);
```
sam: also add a small heuristic: if router shows `x-rw-cache-credit` but econ ingest lacks it, compute estimated_credit = min(estimated_kv_savings, token_cost*0.8) and mark backfill as `estimated`. emit audit events so accounting can reconcile later.
ops: please pause the quota ramp for the Canary bucket until we validate the backfill results. releasing more traffic will make the noise worse.
releasebot: action queued: pause-ramp canary/beta-gnome (reason: econ-credit-investigation)
lina: UX quick win: add a hover tooltip on the new `post_credit_unit_cost` column explaining the math and linking to the reconciliation job run id. mark rows with estimated credits in orange.
mika: tests: econ-tests should simulate header rename and missing header cases, assert credits are applied after mapping/backfill. add an integration case that runs the backfill against a 1h synthetic window.
dev: i'll file the follow-up tickets: ENG-7201 (header-mapping + backfill), ENG-7202 (dashboard post-credit UX), ENG-7203 (econ-tests regression).
ops: once backfill completes, if net billed cost changes > 0.5% for any tenant, we should do a short blameless postmortem and notify finance/customer success.
mika: thanks everyone. i'll add an annotation to the dashboard for the window 2026-04-06T14:00:00Z - 2026-04-06T14:50:00Z and start the ENG-7201 patch. ping me for UX review. :clap:
